scope: tool_executor must not report success when no MCP client is configured
PostgreSQL indexes must report their key columns instead of an empty list
FeedbackAgent and POST /api/v1/feedback must agree on where feedback is stored
a skipped tool step must not be routed into execution_result

item_1_tool_executor.defect: without an MCP client the agent returned _ok({'stub': True, ...}) with status=DONE, so a caller could not tell an unexecuted tool from a completed one
item_1_tool_executor.change: _error('No MCP client configured; {server}.{tool} was not called') with server/tool in metadata; data stays None so no later layer can read it as a result
item_1_tool_executor.not_added: no structured error code — AgentResult only carries errors: list[str], adding a code field would change every agent's serialisation

item_2_postgres_indexes.defect: indexes were read from pg_indexes.indexdef; is_unique was guessed from the text and columns was hardcoded to [] with the comment 'Parsing indexdef is complex; stub for now'
item_2_postgres_indexes.change: query pg_index, join pg_class/pg_namespace, CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series(1, ix.indnkeyatts), array_agg(pg_get_indexdef(ix.indexrelid, k.ord, true) ORDER BY k.ord) as columns, ix.indisunique as is_unique
boundaries: key columns only (indnkeyatts); INCLUDE columns are excluded
expression indexes return the expression text, not a bare column name
public schema only, matching the previous WHERE clause

real_db_assertion.assertion: orders_user_idx.columns == ['user_id'] and is_unique is False, for both PostgreSQL and MySQL fixtures

local_evidence.limitation: tests/test_db does not open a real PostgreSQL connection, so the new SQL is not exercised locally

item_2_postgres_indexes.ci_evidence: produced only by the Real database acceptance workflow (postgres:16 service)

item_3_feedback_paths.defect: the REST route wrote to MySQL and fed the learning collector while the agent only appended to a process-local list; both answered 'recorded', and the agent docstring still said 'Phase 4: stub'

change.agent: writes through MySQLStore.save_feedback with a 9-field row mapping identical to the REST route, reports storage/persisted, records persist_error, sets learning_pipeline=False
change.rest: response gains storage/persisted/learning and a message chosen from the actual storage x learning combination
change.feedback_id: agent rows use fb_agent_{uuid4 hex[:16]} because a per-process counter restarts at zero and would violate uk_feedback_id

item_3_feedback_paths.deliberately_unchanged: status stays 'recorded' — the in-process list really does hold the record, /feedback/stats and /feedback/recent read from it, and the workspace page branches on res.status === 'recorded' in three places
item_3_feedback_paths.before_fix: 8 failed, 14 passed (verified by stashing both source files and rerunning the same two files)

item_4_skip_routing.defect: _stub_result returned status=DONE with {'stub': True}, and _synthesize stored any dict under execution_result — which nodes/respond.py reads as has_result
item_4_skip_routing.change: _stub_result -> _skip_result with {'skipped': True, 'reason': ...}; _synthesize routes skip markers to tool_skipped and only real results to execution_result
item_4_skip_routing.not_changed: no SKIPPED member added to AgentStatus — SPEC §4.11.3 defines only IDLE/BUSY/DONE/ERROR and adding a member is a contract change
item_4_skip_routing.before_fix: 2 of 3 fail on the old tree (the third fails as ImportError because _skip_result does not exist there)

verification.ruff: ruff check app/ tests/ -> All checks passed
verification.mypy: mypy app/ -> no issues in 191 source files (strict unchanged)

not_covered: the feedback MySQL write has not been exercised against a real MySQL server — tests use a fake store, and the Real database acceptance workflow covers tests/real_db, not the feedback endpoint
the learning pipeline still runs only on the REST path; the agent reports learning_pipeline=False instead of running it
field sets are not unified: the collector's SQLite table has diff_count/diff_summary/execution_success, the MySQL feedback table has none of them, and the agent's computed diff only reaches metadata
the REST route still builds feedback_id from a process counter plus a second-resolution timestamp
the seven dialect adapters, real-model capacity, and business accuracy gaps from stages 44-49 are unchanged
